Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨0,\,3{x}^{2}y+2z,\,0⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of the rectangular solid shown above in the first octant. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that only the $y$-component of $F=⟨0,\,3{x}^{2}y+2z,\,0⟩$ is non-zero. Since the lateral sides of $S$ are parallel to the $y$-axis, the flux of $F$ through $S$ will be non-zero only at the right and left sides. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068126/assets/8652a197f603c517cd462c69473e3a693ba8dcd76340b6241f890663356e00cb.png)

 

Let's consider the flux of $F$ through these two sides.

- Let ${S}_{1}$ denote the right surface. On this surface, we have $y=2$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le z\le 1.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{1}$ is

$$
{n}_{1}=⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $y=2$ on ${S}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot {n}_{1} & =⟨0,\,3{x}^{2}y+2z,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6{x}^{2}+2z,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =6{x}^{2}+2z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across ${S}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot {n}_{1}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}6{x}^{2}+2z\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}6{x}^{2}+2z\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}6{x}^{2}+2z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[2{x}^{3}+2xz]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}16+4z\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[16z+2{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$

- Let ${S}_{2}$ denote the left surface. On this surface, we have $y=0$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le z\le 1.$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector to ${S}_{2}$ is

$$
{n}_{2}=⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $y=0$ on ${S}_{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot {n}_{2} & =⟨0,\,3{x}^{2}y+2z,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2z,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =-2z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across ${S}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot {n}_{2}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}-2z\,\text{d}S \\  & =-2{∬}_{D}z\,\text{d}A \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z \\  & =-2\cdot [x]_{0}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2\cdot 2\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & =18+(-2) \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
